full_judgment:
2. The facts, leading to the filing of this appeal, in brief, are that the plaintiff instituted Other Class Suit No. 144 of 1989 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Sadar, Bogra for specific performance of contract alleging, inter alia, that Khairat Ali Mir was the owner of 0551/3 cents of land and the shop standing there on the eastern portion of plot No. 1370 appertaining to modified record of right No. 942 and CS Khatian No. 695 of Mouza-Sutrapur, District-Bogra. After the death of Khairat Ali Mir, his sons and daughters made an amicable family arrangement and according to that family arrangement, Mohammad Ali Mir got the said land and the suit shop. Abdul Halim Tarafder, father of the plaintiff was a monthly tenant in the shop standing on the suit property and he used to run his business in the shop on payment of rent through receipt. After the death of his father, the plaintiff taking consent from his co-sharers started business as usual in the suit shop. Defendant No. 1 proposed selling the suit property including suit shop and the plaintiff agreed to purchase and the price was settled at Taka 40,000 only. On 10-1-1987, defendant No. 1 accepted Taka 37,500 and executed a bainapatra in favour of the plaintiff. It was stipulated that defendant No.1 would register the deed in favour of the plaintiff within two years and a half upon receiving the balance amount of Taka 2500 and it was also stipulated that the plaintiff would continue to make payment of rent of the suit property until the deed of sale was registered. Defendant No. 1 fraudulently instituted Small Cause Court Suit No. 5 of 1988 in the Small Cause Court, Bogra against the mother of the plaintiff for eviction and for realization of arrears of rent and the plaintiff got that suit contested by his mother. Being aware of the said Small Cause Court Suit No. 5 of 1988, the plaintiff on 25-1-1989 requested defendant No. 1 to execute and register the deed of sale on accepting the balance amount of Taka 2500 but he refused to do so. Thereafter, the plaintiff filed the instant suit. 

 3. Defendant No. 1 contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material statements made in the plaint contending, inter-alia, that Khairat Ali Mir brought Partition Suit No. 38 of 1935 in the Court of the then .d an amount of Taka 500 from Khairat Ali Mir. Accordingly, Nasiruddin was given a saham for 0166 cents of land and the balance remained under possession of Khairat Ali Mir who got 0166 cents of land in plot No. 1370 for which a new khatian being Khatain No. 942 was opened in his name. Nasiruddin sold a portion of his land to Baju Mir by a registered deed dated 2-7-1942 and with a view to suppressing the truth defendant No.3 filed the registered deed dated 2-7-1942 after removing two of its pages. During the period of erstwhile Pakistan, Abdul Halim Tarafder, father of the plaintiff, entered into the suit shop as a monthly tenant at a rental of Taka 40 only from Khairat Ali Mir. Abdul Halim Tarafder became the tenant in the suit shop under Ahmed Ali Mir, Ramjan Ali Mir, Khorshed Ali Mir and Mohammad Ali Mir, the four sons of Khairat Ali Mir after his death. After the death of Abdul Halim Tarafder, his wife Sobeda Khatun expressed her desire to continue the business of her husband by remaining in the suit shop as a monthly tenant and accordingly she took the suit shop on rental basis afresh from this defendant and his brothers at a monthly rent of Taka 90 only from December 1977. In 1981 there was an amicable family arrangement among the heirs of late Khairat Ali Mir and in that amicable arrange-merit, the three brothers, namely, Mohammad Ali Mir, Khorshed Ali Mir and Ahmed Ali Mir got the aforesaid 0166 cents and the suit shop standing thereon in equal shares. As the suit shop was required for their own use and as repair works in the suit shop were badly required and as the plaintiff's mother was a habitual defaulter, the defendant and his brothers requested her to vacate the suit shop but she turned a deaf ear to their request. After that, the defendant filed Petition No.1088 (g)86-87 dated 6-11-1986 to the Chairman of Bogra Municipality seeking permission for repairing the suit shop. On 25-11-1986, the plaintiff on behalf of his mother filed a written objection against the said prayer and requested the Chairman, Bogra Municipality for holding an enquiry. After due enquiry, the Chairman had given a direction to Mohammad Ali on 10-1-1987 to take steps for ejectment of tenant and for realization of arrears of rent. The plaintiff's mother did not vacate the suit shop and she was served with a notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act on 4-5-1988. After that, Khorshid Ali Mir and defendant on 10-7-1988 filed Small Cause Court Suit No. 5 of 1988 in the Small Cause Court, Bogra against plaintiff's mother for ejectment and for arrears of rents. When the plaintiff understood that lie would no longer be able to keep the suit shop under his possession, he with the help of his shrewd uncle and dishonest deed writer created the alleged bainapatra by forging the signatures of the defendant on an antedated stamp and cartridge paper. The alleged bainapatra is false, forged, fabricated and antedated and the defendant did not execute any such bainapatra nor did he accept any amount towards the consideration, for the suit shop. As soon as defendant No. 1 came to know about the alleged bainapatra, he filed a complaint in the Court of the Magistrate, Bogra against its writer, witnesses and others under sections 467 and 109 of the Penal Code. In 1987, the market value of the suit property was three to four lacs taka and, as such, value as shown in the agreement at Taka 40,0000 was improbable and shockingly low. Defendant No. 3 (step brother of defendant No. 1's father) and the plaintiff are sailing in the same boat and though he had no interest in the suit property he got himself added as defendant in the suit to help the plaintiff. The claim of the plaintiff is entirely false and the agreement is a forged one and, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed.
